title: Two near-identical 90-line host-grid loaders and a 4x-duplicated password-migration block that must stay in lockstep
existing_state: RestoreApplicationState (Form1.cs:14782-14889) and LoadEnvironmentIntoGrid (Form1.cs:2242-2337) are parallel implementations of the same operation — clear grid, rebuild columns, EnsureSelectColumn, per-row plaintext-password → Credential Manager migration, populate cells, restore checked indices, request refreshes — differing only in input shape (ApplicationState vs EnvironmentConfig) and small drift (the environment loader dedupes/filters columns at :2264-2273; the state loader doesn't). The credential-migration kernel (TryGetValue Host_IP/username/password → resolvedUsername falls back to tsbUsername.Text → StoreHostPassword → blank the cell) is additionally copy-pasted in MigratePasswordsToCredentialManager (Form1.cs:1506-1522) and BuildApplicationState (Form1.cs:14718-14752). The credential key (CredentialTargets.HostPasswordTarget(host, username), Form1.cs:1497) depends on that exact resolution logic — if one copy changes (e.g. trimming, case rules, a new vault_path bypass) and the others don't, stored passwords silently stop resolving for hosts loaded through the other path. Any new convention column or grid semantic must be hand-applied in 2-4 places.
recommendation: Extract two helpers: PopulateHostGrid(IReadOnlyList<string> columns, IEnumerable<IDictionary<string,string>> rows, IReadOnlyList<int> selectedIndices) carrying all the grid mechanics, and MigrateRowPasswordToCredentialManager(IDictionary<string,string> row) carrying the single canonical host+username keying. Have RestoreApplicationState, LoadEnvironmentIntoGrid, BuildApplicationState, and MigratePasswordsToCredentialManager call them. This is also where any bulk-row AddRange/column-index-map performance fix lands once instead of twice.
user_benefit: One place to change grid/credential semantics instead of four — removes the class of bug where an environment-loaded fleet and a state-restored fleet behave differently (including stored passwords silently not resolving).
